detail.readme:
![screenshot of cv.jarocki.me, a CV built with this template](.github/screenshot.png)

minimalist cv

[![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-16-black?logo=next.js)](https://nextjs.org/) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.9-blue?logo=typescript)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-3.4-38B2AC?logo=tailwind-css)](https://tailwindcss.com/) simple web app that renders a minimalist CV with print-friendly layout. maintained by an ai robot 🤖, with a human pressing merge. ## requirements - node 22.15 or later. `pnpm verify` refuses to run on older versions. - pnpm ## getting started ```bash git clone https://github.com/BartoszJarocki/cv.git cd cv pnpm install pnpm dev # open http://localhost:3000 # edit src/data/resume-data.ts to customize ``` ## scripts ```bash pnpm dev # start development server pnpm build # build for production pnpm start # start production server pnpm lint # run biome linting checks pnpm lint:fix # run biome linting with auto-fix pnpm format # check code formatting with biome pnpm format:fix # format code with biome pnpm check # run both linting and formatting checks pnpm check:fix # run both linting and formatting with auto-fix pnpm verify # check the page, text and markdown that pnpm build prerendered ``` ## project structure ``` scripts/ └── verify.mjs # checks run by pnpm verify src/ ├── app/ # next.js app router │ ├── components/ # page-level components │ │ ├── education.tsx │ │ ├── header.tsx │ │ ├── projects.tsx │ │ ├── skills.tsx │ │ ├── summary.tsx │ │ └── work-experience.tsx │ ├── index.md/ │ │ └── route.ts # the CV as markdown │ ├── index.txt/ │ │ └── route.ts # the CV as text, for curl │ ├── llms.txt/ │ │ └── route.ts # the markdown, with a note on the formats │ ├── apple-icon.png # home screen icon │ ├── favicon.ico # browser tab icon │ ├── globals.css # color palette and base styles │ ├── layout.tsx # root layout with metadata │ ├── opengraph-image.tsx │ ├── page.tsx # main resume page │ ├── robots.ts │ └── sitemap.ts ├── components/ # shared components │ ├── icons/ # social icon components │ ├── ui/ # presentational components │ ├── command-menu-dialog.tsx │ └── command-menu.tsx ├── data/ # resume data configuration │ ├── avatar.jpg # your photo │ └── resume-data.ts └── lib/ # utilities and types ├── document.ts # the CV as blocks for the text and markdown ├── markdown.ts ├── resume.ts ├── structured-data.ts ├── text.ts ├── types.ts └── utils.ts ``` ## customization all resume content lives in a single file: ```typescript // src/data/resume-data.ts export const RESUME_DATA = { name: "Your Name", location: "Your City, Country", siteUrl: "https://cv.example.com", // where this CV is deployed about: "One line under your name", // also the meta description and share image text summary: "A paragraph for the About section", // ... more fields } export const SECTION_TITLES = { summary: "About", work: "Work Experience", // ... education, skills, projects } ``` `SECTION_TITLES`, in the same file, holds the section headings. to rename or translate a section, change its heading there. the sections appear in the order of its keys, and the page skips any section whose data is empty, such as `projects: []`. replace `src/data/avatar.jpg` with your own square photo, a jpeg or a png. to use another file name, put the file directly in `src/data` and change the avatar import in `src/data/resume-data.ts`. replace `src/app/favicon.ico` and `src/app/apple-icon.png` with your own icons. next.js links them by file name, so no config is needed. styling uses tailwind css. the palette is six oklch color roles in `src/app/globals.css`, one set for light and one for dark. `tailwind.config.js` maps the tailwind color names onto those roles. `src/app/opengraph-image.tsx` and the `themeColor` list in `src/app/layout.tsx` set their own hex colors, so a palette change in `globals.css` does not reach the share image or the browser theme color. ## text and markdown the CV also comes as text for terminals and as markdown for ai agents: ```bash curl https://cv.jarocki.me # 80-column text curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://cv.jarocki.me # markdown curl https://cv.jarocki.me/index.md # markdown, for any client curl https://cv.jarocki.me/llms.txt # markdown, with a note on the formats ``` - curl, httpie and xh get the text at `/`. wget and browsers get the html page. - the text uses ansi bold and dim. to page through it, pipe it to `less -R`. - ai agents that ask for markdown with `Accept: text/markdown` get it at `/`. the html page also links it with ``. - `/index.txt` serves the text to any client, such as `wget -qO- https://cv.jarocki.me/index.txt`. the text and the markdown come from `src/data/resume-data.ts`, like the page, so they change when you edit it. `pnpm build` renders them as static files, and `pnpm verify` checks them against the data. the rewrites in `next.config.js` pick the version for `/`. to serve the text to another tool, add its user agent to the `user-agent` pattern there. to try it locally, run `pnpm dev` and `curl http://localhost:3000`. a plain `curl cv.jarocki.me` gets vercel's redirect from http to https and prints `Redirecting...`. use `https://`, or `curl -L`. ##
